label: prop:reeb-pn-magnitude-criticality
title: Deformed exchange criticality: $g^2\,(1+[2]_v^2)=1$ characterizes the pn-bond magnitude, with $5+(v-v^{-1})^2 = 1+[2]_v^2$
html:
Let R be a commutative ring, v \in R invertible, [2]_v = v + v^{-1}, and let

\begin{align*}
  M(b) &= \begin{pmatrix} 1 & b \\ b & -1 \end{pmatrix},
  &S(a,w) &= \begin{pmatrix}
     0 & a & w & w\\
     a & 0 & w & w\\
     w & w & 0 & -a\\
     w & w & -a & 0
  \end{pmatrix}
\end{align*}

denote the symmetric-sector exchange matrix and the uniform-magnitude [1^4] complete-graph exchange matrix on nucleon blocks [p,p,n,n]. Then:

  1. (Deformation identity) 5 + (v - v^{-1})^2 = 1 + [2]_v^2.
  2. (Cayley–Hamilton form) M(b)^2 = (1 + b^2)\cdot\mathbf{1}; in particular the classical b = 2 gives the scalar 5.
  3. (Marginal stability) \det\bigl(\mathbf{1} + g\,M(b)\bigr) = 1 - g^2(1+b^2) for every b; hence, specializing to the deformed pn-degree b = [2]_v, any g with g^2(1 + [2]_v^2) = 1 is exactly the point where the deformed symmetric-sector determinant \det\bigl(\mathbf{1} + g\,M([2]_v)\bigr) vanishes.
  4. (pn-sign blindness) With D = \mathrm{diag}(1,1,-1,-1) one has D\,S(a,w)\,D = S(a,-w), and consequently \det(\mathbf{1} + S(a,w)) = \det(\mathbf{1} + S(a,-w)) and \mathrm{tr}\bigl(T\,S(a,w)^k\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}\bigl(T\,S(a,-w)^k\bigr) for every k and every T commuting with D.

In particular the magnitude g with g^2(1+[2]_v^2) = 1 equals z/\sqrt{1+z^2} evaluated at the Markov bond factor z = 1/[2]_v whenever square roots are available, and satisfies g^2\,(5 + (v-v^{-1})^2) = 1 by item 1.

Scope

The proposition is pure exchange-matrix algebra; it carries no physical identification. The physical reading of g as the pn-bond linking amplitude is the separate conjecture. Item 4 implies the [1^4] pn writhe sign is invisible to every grading-commuting observable class; sign sensitivity requires p{\leftrightarrow}n mixing operators.
